crop.notes: Column spliced from the bottom of one column to the top of the next; a line or so is lost at the join ('Mike McCool, the terror of the ... feated him'). Allen passage complete.

ocr.notes: Mostly right; 'Bill Rayel' rendered as 'Bill =' and a few words garbled at the splice.

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Republic marked the death of Joe Coburn with a career profile, noting that before his match with Jem Mace in England, Mace's party pitted Joe Goss, Tom Allen and Bill Rayel against Coburn, who bested them all.

metadata.notes: Masthead: The Republic: St. Louis, Mo., Monday Morning, December 8, 1890, page 5.

facts.fact: In England, before Joe Coburn's championship match with Jem Mace, the Mace party pitted Joe Goss, Tom Allen and Bill Rayel against Coburn to test him; Coburn bested them all

notes: Retrospective obituary of Coburn; no date given for the trials. Article 804 (McManus) dates the Coburn-Mace match to 1868 and spells the third man 'Bill Rayne'.
